This explanation is not quite right. I checked it with the activation check from `main`, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit:

- `isFocusable()` already fails while the overlay is still open. `offsetParent` is `null` for select, context-menu and menu-bar items, and for a button or field placed directly in a dialog or popover. It is not `null` for combo-box and time-picker items, or for content inside a positioned wrapper.
- `:focus-within` fails because closing the overlay restores focus to the element that had it before, which can be outside the cell. For an overlay that stays open, it fails in Chromium and WebKit, where `:focus-within` does not match through an open popover.
- It is not limited to overlays opened from code. An item of a context menu opened from non-focusable cell content activates the row too. So does a button in a popover that stays open, in Chromium and WebKit.

```suggestion
     * True when the click path reaches the cell through a popover element
     * (e.g. a Vaadin overlay) rendered inside that cell. Popover content is
     * rendered in the top layer, where the focus and visibility based checks
     * in `_shouldPreventCellActivationOnClick` are not reliable. Ancestors
     * outside the cell are ignored, so a grid inside an overlay still
     * activates its cells.
```

comments.body:
Thanks for the review, @tomivirkki. I replaced the `*-overlay` tag name check with `node.popover` (Vaadin overlays are `popover="manual"`, so this also covers a native popover rendered in a cell). The select overlay case now lives in `test/integration/grid-select.test.js`, using the real `vaadin-select` opened without focus. `dialog-grid.test.js` has a regression test that cells of a grid inside a dialog still activate. `events.test.js` keeps one test for a native `<div popover="manual">`.

This response was drafted with assistance from Claude Code.

Thanks @web-padawan. Shortened the comment in `_shouldPreventCellActivationOnClick` and moved the rationale into the `__isClickInsideCellOverlay` JSDoc (f346a11).

On whether the other checks already cover this: they don't for these two cases. When an item in an overlay is clicked, the overlay closes synchronously, so `_isFocusable(e.target)` no longer sees an element with an `offsetParent`. And `:focus-within` on the cell content misses overlays opened from code, where focus never entered the cell. The path check covers both, and only looks at nodes between the target and the cell, so a grid placed inside an overlay still activates its own cells (covered in `dialog-grid.test.js`). If you'd rather drop it, I can, but the select integration test fails without it.

This response was drafted with assistance from Claude Code.

Thanks for checking this across browsers and for correcting the explanation. Applied the suggested external focus, second-item selection and value assertion, public DOM queries, mouse cleanup, sinon-chai assertions, native popover markup, and module-level helper with the supplied JSDoc. Removed the redundant timeout.

This response was drafted with assistance from an AI assistant.

Thanks @tomivirkki. I updated the PR description to match the current implementation: the `node.popover` check in the `isInsideCellPopover` helper (instead of the `-overlay` tag name check) and the test locations (select integration test, dialog-grid regression, native popover case in `events.test.js`).

This response was drafted with assistance from Claude Code.
